tagline.text: Whale sharks and coral reefs at the quiet southern tip of Sogod Bay

location.label: Location
location.text: Southern tip of Southern Leyte: Liloan, Pintuyan, San Francisco and San Ricardo

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: November–May (March–April is often rated best for whale sharks)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱4,000~10,000 (estimate for 2 days 1 night, including lodging, tour and transport; confirm locally)

children.text: Panaon Island is a long island at the very south of Southern Leyte, where whale-shark watching, diving and quiet coastal villages come together. In 2025 the surrounding waters were declared the Panaon Island Protected Seascape, bringing even more attention to its coral reefs.
Panaon Island extends from the southern end of Leyte, about
30km
long from north to south with an area of roughly
191km²

. Dinagat Island lies to the east and Mindanao to the southeast across the Surigao Strait, the Bohol (Mindanao) Sea lies to the west and Sogod Bay to the northwest. The island has four municipalities, Liloan, Pintuyan, San Francisco and San Ricardo, and Liloan is the largest town. The highest point is Mount Nelangcapan at about 698 m. The population was around 57,000 in 2015, and most villages live from coconuts, rice and fishing.

What makes Panaon special for travelers is the sea. Whale sharks, which local fishers call "tikitiki," visit the waters around the island, and there are healthy coral reefs, walls draped in huge gorgonian sea fans and channel dive sites with strong currents. An Oceana expedition in 2020 reportedly found coral cover of at least 60 percent in places, about three times the national average (Oceana puts that at around 20 percent).

When Republic Act No. 12238 was signed in late August 2025, the waters around the island became the Panaon Island Protected Seascape. Reports describe an area of roughly 60,000 hectares, and there is news that a protected area management board has been formed and a management plan approved. Rules may differ by municipality, so check the latest notices from each town's tourism office before you visit.

There are no large resorts or shopping malls here yet, so facilities are simple. The island suits slow travel along the coastal road, with stops at village markets, piers, waterfalls and viewpoints. Rather than expecting a glitzy resort like Cebu or Bohol, plan it as one leg of a Sogod Bay diving trip or stay 2~3 days for whale sharks and reefs, and you will likely be happy with it. When planning for the first time, decide where to stay first. Pintuyan is the usual base for whale sharks, while Liloan is the base if access to mainland Leyte, the Wawa Bridge and the beaches matters most. San Francisco is a quiet coastal town between the two, and San Ricardo is the southern gateway with boats to Surigao. The coastal road around the island changes character from village to village and is worth a slow day's drive. The island is long and travel takes longer than you expect, so do not try to see every town in one day.
Pintuyan is regarded as the center of whale-shark watching on the island. Local fishers first look for sharks from small bangkas, then you enter the water with a guide. An outing can last up to about
3 hours

, but the animals are wild and some days you will not see one. Guides describe the length differently, so ask your lodging the day before. During the season the first boat out is often recommended, so an early start may work in your favor.

blocks.title: Drift diving at Liloan's Wawa Bridge

children.text: The channel under the steel "Wawa Bridge" linking Liloan to mainland Leyte has strong alternating currents and whirlpools. One story says Liloan takes its name from "lilo," meaning whirlpool. Unless you are an experienced diver, do not go in without a guide.

Dive guides often feature the Napantao sanctuary, with walls covered in huge gorgonian fans. When a current is running, your chances of seeing large pelagic fish improve. It is often combined with diving on the Sogod Bay side. If you are not certified, ask your lodging first whether an introductory dive or snorkeling over shallow reef is possible.
The Tabugon fish sanctuary off Liloan was established in 1993 and is described as covering about 90 hectares. It is known as a place to see manta rays and dolphins, and the seabed drops away steeply.

Liloan has Bituon Beach, Maamo Beach and Molopolo Beach. Molopolo is known as the starting point for island hopping, and Maamo is famous for white sand and clear water. Bangka rates vary a lot by season and negotiation.

Pintuyan has Busay Falls, Catbawan Falls and Dan-an Falls, and the Caningag viewpoints and Son-ok Peak look out over the island and the sea. Road conditions and water flow vary by season, so ask locally.

Liloan Lighthouse is described as a good place to watch the sea at dusk. Along Pintuyan Boulevard on the town's waterfront, barbecue stalls open in the evening, which makes a relaxed meal with the sunset.
Travel to Pintuyan from Tacloban or Maasin. From Tacloban the road distance is about
178km
, so it takes close to half a day.

Drop your bags, then walk around town and take in the pier and the waterfront. Whale-shark tours usually go out early in the morning, so confirm the next day's plan with your lodging or the fishers' association.
Watch the sunset at the barbecue stalls on Pintuyan Boulevard and eat early. After
fewer places stay open, so do not wait.
Head out by bangka for whale-shark watching. First you look for sharks from the boat, then enter the water on the guide's instruction. If you find one, you may stay with it for about
1~3 hours
After lunch, visit a waterfall or viewpoint, or leave early to allow for travel time.
Whale sharks are wild and sightings are not guaranteed. If you can spare another day, your chances improve.
Cross the Wawa Bridge and arrive in Liloan. Look around the beaches, the lighthouse and the small islands reachable by bangka, then watch the sunset.
Travel south from Liloan to Pintuyan, enjoying coastal villages and markets. If you dive, arrange a drift or Napantao dive through a local resort.
Visit Pintuyan's waterfalls or viewpoints, or rest after a whale-shark tour.
Head toward San Ricardo and check boats to Surigao, or return the way you came. Boat times can change, so find out the day before.

items.title: From Manila by plane and road

children.text: Fly from Manila to Tacloban (TAC). Flight times and fares vary by season, so check booking sites.
From Tacloban, take a van or bus south to Panaon Island, passing Sogod and Liloan. Some dive shops describe the transfer from Tacloban as about
3 hours
Van and bus fares to Liloan were ₱150~250 according to a 2011 article. They may have risen since, so confirm locally.
Road conditions can lengthen the trip, so allow plenty of time.
Take a boat from Cebu to a port on Leyte (such as Hilongos), then continue south by van or bus.
Ferry timetables change often, so confirm with the operator before departure.
You can reach San Ricardo by boat from Surigao, and Pintuyan is described as about
15 minutes
from San Ricardo.
From San Ricardo to Pintuyan you can go by van, bus, motorcycle taxi (habal-habal) or tricycle.
On the island, tricycles, habal-habal and resort pickups are the basics. Vans and buses also run between towns.
Public transport is sparse to beaches, waterfalls and viewpoints, so it is easiest to ask your lodging to arrange a vehicle.

Whale sharks are generally described as in season from November to April or May, and many accounts rate March–April as especially good. Some sources say they are seen year-round or from November to July, so confirm the timing with local fishers and your lodging.
Diving is said to be best from October to March, while June–August can be windy with rough seas.

In Pintuyan, Pintuyan Dive Resort is known as a long-established diving and whale-shark base, and there are simple places such as D & G Transient House and La-Guerta Lodging House. Some are not on booking sites, so ask locally. In Liloan, Anilao Hidden Valley Resort, Bayfront Lodge and Beach Resort and Peter's Dive Resort are among those mentioned.

Eating is mostly simple local restaurants and barbecue stalls along the shore. For a snack, ampaw, a sweet rice puff with peanuts, is described as a Panaon specialty. Bring cash, since ATMs and card payments are limited, and withdraw in Tacloban or Maasin beforehand.

Many travelers eat at their lodging. Fish and seafood are available at village markets and resorts can cook what you bring, so tell them what you would like. Evening meal service ends early, so carry snacks and water, and pack lunch on travel days.
If you meet a whale shark, keep your distance and do not touch, chase or block it.
Enter the water quietly and follow the guide's instructions.
Ordinary sunscreen can harm coral, so use a rash guard or a reef-friendly product.
Whale sharks are not guaranteed, so we recommend at least 2 nights.
Carry plenty of cash and a local SIM card.
Plan to finish dinner before
Bus, van and boat times change often, so leave a buffer.
Follow the local advice not to touch anything on the seafloor.
On travel days, leave by morning at the latest so you arrive before dark.
The channel under the Wawa Bridge has strong currents and whirlpools and is dangerous without an expert diver and a guide.
Whale-shark seasons and tourism rules may change from year to year, so check the latest notices before you go.
Bangka trips can be cancelled when the sea is rough.
Do not step on or touch coral and marine life. With the area now protected, rules may become stricter.
Mountain and viewpoint roads are slippery after rain and can be dangerous by motorbike.
Medical and other facilities are limited, so bring medicine and cash.
A bay to the northwest of Panaon Island known for diving and whale-shark watching, easy to combine with a Panaon trip.
Islands across the Surigao Strait that you can fit into a plan together with boats from Surigao.
The city most travelers fly into and the starting point for the overland trip south to Panaon.
